Lifting a family from three restrictions

To recover the morphisms of a generated subcategory, the formalization uses the three endomorphisms of the walking morphism. The calculation is about a whole family of arrows. Here is how its three restrictions are assembled, using specified lifts rather than a choice made separately at every point.

Assume the Chapter 1 mapping-anima and coproduct structures. For a functor \(m\colon X\to Y\), write \(m_*\) for postcomposition on mapping animae. A lift of \(h\) through \(m_*\) includes a functor \(\widetilde h\) and an identification \(m_*\widetilde h=h\).

Supplementary Lemma 1. Let \(h\colon \Gamma \to \Map (A\sqcup B,Y)\), where \(\Gamma \) is any absolute category. If the restrictions of \(h\) to \(A\) and \(B\) have specified lifts through \(m_*\), then \(h\) has a lift through \(\Map (A\sqcup B,X)\to \Map (A\sqcup B,Y)\).

Proof idea

Pair the two supplied lifts and lift this pair through the equivalence \[ \Map (A\sqcup B,X)\iso \Map (A,X)\times \Map (B,X). \] Restriction to the two summands commutes with postcomposition by \(m\). Consequently, the two supplied comparison identifications give an identification of the restrictions of \(m_*\widetilde h\) and \(h\). Reflect it through the corresponding restriction equivalence for \(Y\). This gives the required comparison for the whole family. The argument does not require \(m\) to be an embedding. □

Supplementary Lemma 2. Suppose \(x_0,x_1,x_2\colon \star \to K\) induce an equivalence \((\star \sqcup \star )\sqcup \star \iso K\). A family \(h\colon \Gamma \to \Map (K,Y)\) lifts through \(m_*\) if its three restrictions to \(\Map (\star ,Y)\) have specified lifts.

Proof idea

Apply Supplementary Lemma 1 twice. At each step, transport the supplied comparisons along the computation identifications for the coproduct inclusions. This lifts the restriction of \(h\) along the displayed equivalence. Precomposition by that equivalence is itself an equivalence on mapping animae. Lift back through it and reflect the comparison with \(h\). Notice that the three restrictions take values in \(\Map (\star ,Y)=Y^\simeq \); we keep these core-valued restrictions explicit, rather than identifying \(\Map (\star ,Y)\) with \(Y\). □

Supplementary Lemma 3. Assume also the walking-morphism, endpoint, Segal, commutative-square, interval-core and coproduct-universality structures of the preceding chapters. Let \(m\colon M\hookrightarrow \Map ([1],C)\) be a collection closed under source and target identities, and let \(i\colon A\to C\) be a subcategory presentation of \(M\). The comparison \[ \Map ([1],A)\longrightarrow M \] is an equivalence.

Proof idea

Use the established three-point presentation of \(\Map ([1],[1])\), whose points name the constant functor at \(0\), the identity functor, and the constant functor at \(1\). The family \(M\to \Map ([1],C)\) acts by postcomposition on this anima. Its three restrictions are the source identity, the given arrow, and the target identity. The two closure witnesses supply the first and third lifts; the middle lift is the identity. The naming and evaluation comparisons put these lifts in the form needed by Supplementary Lemma 2.

The resulting lift of the whole action supplies a cone for the defining subcategory pullback, tested at \([1]\). Its factorization gives a section of \(\Map ([1],A)\to M\). The comparison is an embedding because both maps into \(\Map ([1],C)\) are embeddings. An embedding with a section is an equivalence. Closure under composition is needed to obtain the presentation from the subcategory axiom, but this calculation, with a presentation already supplied, uses only closure under identities. □
